Retention windows and operational promises

This synthetic analysis is not legal advice. It examines the engineering meaning of a system that promises to recover asynchronous work after a stated outage.

  1. Evidence. Terminal job records provide facts used to distinguish completed, failed, and missing work.
  2. Duration. The evidence must remain available longer than detection, reconciliation, and supported recovery delays combined.
  3. Disclosure. Deployment documentation should state when finite cleanup is enabled and how rollback changes the required retention setting.

A configuration validator can enforce the arithmetic at startup. An alert should fire before the oldest retained row approaches the minimum safe duration, leaving time for an operator to pause cleanup.

Footnote 1: all names and scenarios in this fixture are fictional.
